CNT-Mediated Integration of Pd and In2O3 Circumvents Activity–Stability Trade-Off in CO2 Hydrogenation to Methanol
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Metal promotion is a widely adopted strategy to enhance the activity of indium oxide (In2O3) catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol. However, intimately contacted metal promoters on In2O3 often result in rapid catalyst deactivation, as excessive local H2 supply induces undesirable structural degradation of the In2O3 domain. Here, we address this limitation by implementing a carbon nanotube (CNT)-mediated hydrogen transport pathway, which spatially separates the H2 activation sites (Pd) from the CO2 hydrogenation sites (In2O3) at the catalyst preparation stage. Intriguingly, upon reductive activation, the initially separated components spontaneously evolve into a distinctive interfacial configuration. In this configuration, InOx migrates onto and partially covers the Pd nanoparticles, forming an InOx@Pd inverse interface. Unlike the directly constructed Pd–In2O3 interface, which suffers from over-reduction to metallic In0 accompanied by sintering and alloying with Pd, this CNT-derived interface preserves the In3+ oxidation state and serves as a non-destructive junction for hydrogen delivery. Combined with long-range hydrogen spillover across the CNT network, this architecture transforms a concentrated and destructive hydrogen flux into a regulated supply that reaches distal In2O3 domains without driving over-reduction. Consequently, the Pd/CNT + In2O3 system exhibits both improved catalytic activity and enhanced long-term stability ( gt;230 h), whereas the conventional Pd/In2O3 catalyst deactivates continuously. These findings demonstrate that a controlled hydrogen delivery system between H2 activation sites and active sites on the oxide domain offers an effective way for developing active and durable catalysts involving reduction-sensitive oxide phases.

missingCandidates.title: Hydration Changes are Essential for Efficient Breakdown of Faropenem by the L1 Metallo-β-lactamase
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. Benchmarking against B3LYP-D3/6-31G(d) shows that DFTB3 provides the best correlation between energy and structure for this system. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. Our results show that a zinc-bridging hydroxide acts as the nucleophile, with the conserved active site residue D120 participating in back-and-forth proton-transfer events and stabilizing the enzyme-intermediate (EI) complex. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. This water molecule was observed during long-timescale MM MD simulations using the Extended Zinc Amber Force Field (EZAFF). Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2. missingCandidates.title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

missingCandidates.title: Controlled Hydrogen Delivery by Single‐Atom Ru Accelerates Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia (NORR) offers a dual opportunity for NO remediation and decentralized NH 3 production, yet its efficiency is often limited by competing pathways and unclear structure–function relationships. Here we introduce a reactant‐shunting strategy that installs a guiding electrocatalytic step via isolated Ru atoms to supply surface‐bound * H species and enforce a Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) hydrogenation pathway. Using Ru 1 /Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst, we show that single Ru sites promote water adsorption and dissociation, forming stable Ru‐H intermediates that thermodynamically and kinetically accelerate the coupling‐hydrogenation steps in NORR. The optimized catalyst delivers an NH 3 yield of 533.49 µmol cm −2 h −1 with a 97.19% faradaic efficiency, surpassing state‐of‐the‐art systems. The reactant‐shunting principle further generalizes across multiple oxide hosts, enhancing NH 3 productivity by up to threefold. These findings establish pathway steering through controlled hydrogen delivery as a powerful strategy for high‐efficiency electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis.

missingCandidates.title: Double Reduction of Ph 3 B to a Dianionic Borane With a Powerful Sr I Intermediate
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Reduction of [(BDI)SrI] 2 with KC 8 generated in situ a (BDI)Sr I species which enabled the reduction of Ph 3 B to the Ph 3 B 2− dianion (BDI = HC[(Me)C═N‐DIPeP] 2 , DIPeP = 2,6‐(Et 2 CH) 2 ‐phenyl). The product (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) features a Ph 3 B 2− dianion that is bridging two Sr 2+ cations by interaction with one of the Ph rings. This polarizes a large part of the electron density in the bridging Ph ring (NPA charge: −1.53) whereas the B is slightly positive (+0.44). The HOMO of the complex mainly consists of the π*‐orbital in the bridging Ph ring overlapping with Sr d ‐orbitals. However, there is also 18% contribution of the B p ‐orbital. In solution, there is coalescence of 1 H NMR signals of all three Ph rings. Complex (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) can react as a 2 e transfer reagent or as a B‐nucleophile. It reacts with I 2 to Ph 3 B and [(BDI)SrI] 2 . Reaction with Ph 3 B led to formation of a Gomberg‐type dimer. The reaction with PhI is smooth and selectively gave (BDI)Sr(Ph 4 B) and [(BDI)SrI] 2 , likely through direct nucleophilic attack of an electron rich B atom at PhI. Isolation of a complex with the elusive Ph 3 B 2− dianion demonstrates the very high reducing power of in situ generated (BDI)Sr I species.

missingCandidates.title: In Situ and Operando Techniques for Electrocatalysis in Renewable Energy Applications
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding closed‐loop experimentation, data‐driven approaches promise to reduce reliance on empirical trial‐and‐error and unlock predictive control over catalytic performance. Taken together, these developments position operando characterization, when coupled with AI‐driven interpretation, as a cornerstone of future energy research, providing a pathway to accelerate discovery, design, and deployment of next‐gen

missingCandidates.title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

missingCandidates.title: Overcoming the Spin Barrier of Oxygen Redox Chemistry in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries via Metal–Support Magnetic Interaction
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT A major bottleneck for the practical application of lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries is the high overpotential resulting from sluggish kinetics of oxygen redox chemistry. This kinetic limitation can rise in part from the spin‐state transition barriers in converting triplet oxygen ( 3 O 2 ) into peroxide species, alongside the parasitic generation of singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). Here, we demonstrate that metal–support magnetic interactions can effectively overcome this spin barrier. Using palladium (Pd) nanoparticles anchored on ferrimagnetic CoFe 2 O 4 (CFO) substrates as a model catalyst, we reveal that interfacial magnetic coupling restructures the spin and electronic states of Pd sites, generating spin‐polarized active ensembles with optimized adsorption toward oxygen intermediates. This interfacial spin‐electronic effect promotes the conversion of 3 O 2 into peroxide species while suppressing parasitic 1 O 2 evolution during charging, thereby improving the reversibility of oxygen redox chemistry. As a result, the Pd/CFO catalyst achieves a low charging overpotential of 0.05 V and remarkable energy efficiency (91.2%) under spin alignment. This finding establishes metal–support magnetic interaction as a powerful strategy for controlling spin‐dependent oxygen electrocatalysis, providing a general design principle for catalysts involving multi‐site interactions.

missingCandidates.title: Persistent Mn 3+ Sites on Reduced MnO Enable Efficient Syngas Conversion
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based materials are widely used for syngas conversion, where MnO is generally regarded as the catalytically active phase under reducing conditions. Yet catalysts derived from different Mn oxide precursors often exhibit markedly different performances despite evolving into the same MnO bulk structure during reaction. Here we show that trace Mn 3+ sites stabilized on oxygen‐deficient MnO surfaces serve as the decisive active sites. Time‐resolved energy‐dispersive x‐ray absorption spectroscopy combined with iterative target transformation factor analysis and depth‐resolved synchrotron photoemission spectroscopy reveals a persistent minor Mn 3 O 4 ‐like spectral contribution and its enrichment near the surface of Mn 2 O 3 ‐derived MnO. These stabilized sites strongly enhance CO adsorption and activation, thereby promoting C─O bond cleavage and markedly improving activity and selectivity for syngas‐to‐light‐olefin conversion. More broadly, this work reveals how minority surface sites can govern catalytic function despite identical bulk phases and establishes an operando strategy for quantitatively resolving low‐coverage active sites in reducible oxide catalysts.

missingCandidates.title: RNA Organelles in DNA‐Based Artificial Cells Provide Spatial Aptamer Functions and Enhanced Signal Processing
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Naturally occurring biomolecular condensates orchestrate key cellular processes by creating spatially distinct reaction environments, yet engineering synthetic condensates that combine structural programmability with spatioselectively encoded function remains challenging. Here, we report multiphase DNA–RNA artificial cells (ACs) that embed functional RNA condensates as organelle‐like compartments within programmable DNA core–shell ACs. A single thermal assembly protocol yields three‐phase ACs comprising a glassy RNA core organelle embedded in a liquid‐like DNA compartment, surrounded by a crosslinked DNA shell. The RNA organelles contain aptamer function, enabling selective protein recruitment and small‐molecule activation, while the DNA scaffold provides independent addressability, modulates RNA‐condensate size, and enhances resistance to serum‐mediated degradation. We further show that RNA chemistry can be used to adjust environmental responsiveness: unmodified RNA organelles undergo rapid degradation in serum and release captured protein cargo, whereas 2′‐fluoro‐modified RNA organelles remain stable for at least 24 h. Finally, by coupling transcriptional modules localized in the DNA core to cell‐free protein translation in the surrounding medium, we establish sender–receiver communication between AC populations and self‐actuating signal processing within individual DNA–RNA ACs. These results establish hybrid nucleic‐acid ACs as programmable, spatially organized systems that couple compartment architecture, RNA molecular recognition, and biochemical communication.

missingCandidates.title: Stabilizing Functional Nucleic Acids for Real‐Sample Diagnostics
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional nucleic acids (FNAs), including aptamers and DNAzymes, offer programmable recognition and catalysis for biosensing, but their performance in real samples is often compromised by nuclease degradation, matrix effects, and interface‐associated losses. For diagnostic translation, stability must, therefore, be defined not only as strand persistence, but as retained folding, binding, catalysis, and signal generation under assay‐relevant conditions. This review examines strategies for stabilizing FNAs in complex biological matrices and organizes the field around four design levers: Chemical, topological, architectural, and microenvironment/interface engineering. Chemical modification of sugars, backbones, and bases can reduce nuclease susceptibility, but requires functional validation. Topological approaches, including terminus shielding, circularization, covalent locking, and mechanically interlocked structures, limit strand accessibility, and reinforce functional conformations. Architectural strategies use multivalency, scaffolded presentation, DNA nanostructures, and rolling circle amplification‐derived concatemers to improve robustness and signal retention. Microenvironment engineering further stabilizes FNAs through controlled immobilization, antifouling interfaces, nanomaterial‐assisted protection, hydrogel or microgel confinement, and sample processing. Case studies in saliva, serum, urine, and stool illustrate how these levers can be combined to enable reliable FNA‐based real‐sample diagnostics.

missingCandidates.title: Structural Softness–Rigidity Mediation Enables Multicolor Emission and Long‐Lived Phosphorescence in Hf/Zr Halides
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Multicolor fluorescence, typically favored by soft environments, and phosphorescence, which relies on rigid lattices to stabilize triplet excitons, are fundamentally incompatible and hard to coexist within a single material. Here, we report a crown–ether–directed lattice assembly that integrates [HfCl 6 ] 2‒ /[ZrCl 6 ] 2‒ octahedra and DB18C6@M(K + /Rb + ) supramolecular, yielding four unknown organic–inorganic hybrid Hf/Zr halides. Notably, (DB18C6@K) 2 (CH 3 CN) 2 HfCl 6 achieves an exceptional room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) quantum yield (Φ p ) of 54.43%, a long lifetime of 0.8 s, and a visually discernible afterglow persisting up to 6 s. Moreover, these materials exhibit excitation–dependent multicolor emission, producing green and blue–white outputs under 302 and 365 nm irradiation, respectively. This unique multimodal luminescence originates from the synergistic interplay between the balanced soft‐rigid lattice provided by the crown‐ether framework and heavy – atom Hf/Zr centers, which facilitates intersystem crossing, enabling both efficient RTP and tunable multichannel pathways. It has been confirmed by the high–pressure synchrotron angle–dispersive x–ray diffraction and Raman results. Overall, this work establishes a heavy–atom–based structural mediation which may offer a generalizable route to high‐efficiency, multichannel, and stimuli‐responsive RTP materials.

missingCandidates.title: Topological Engineering of NIR‐II Emissive Conjugated Oligomers With Unexpected Excited‐State Manifolds for Efficient Phototheranostics and Cancer Immunotherapy
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Phototheranostic agents operating in the second near‐infrared (NIR‐II) window hold great potential for precision cancer therapy, yet the rational regulation of excited‐state processes to simultaneously optimize fluorescence and phototherapeutic performances remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report a topology‐driven excited‐state engineering strategy for constructing conjugated oligomers with tailored excited‐state manifolds and multi‐channel excitation dynamics. By precisely manipulating molecular topology, conjugated topological oligomers achieve enhanced light‐harvesting capability and optimized exciton utilization, thereby enabling synergistic regulation of excitation dynamics. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, nanoparticles (NPs) derived from TBT‐3 exhibit 2.8‐fold enhanced NIR‐II fluorescence brightness, 2.7‐fold improved photothermal performance, and 7.5‐fold increased total reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation compared with TBT‐1. In vivo studies demonstrate that TBT‐3 NPs enable high‐resolution NIR‐II fluorescence imaging and efficient tumor elimination. Moreover, TBT‐3‐mediated phototherapy induces immunogenic cell death and enhances antitumor immunity, leading to improved therapeutic efficacy when combined with anti‐PD‐1 immune checkpoint blockade. This work provides a molecular topology‐based strategy for manipulating excited‐state landscapes and establishes conjugated oligomers as versatile candidates for NIR‐II phototheranostics and cancer immunotherapy.

missingCandidates.title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

missingCandidates.title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

missingCandidates.title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

missingCandidates.title: Deciphering Interheme Electron-Transfer Pathways in a Diheme Peroxidase from Methane-Oxidizing Bacteria
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Bis-FeIV-forming enzymes represent an emerging paradigm in high-valent heme iron chemistry, in which two hemes separated by 15–20 Å are both oxidized to the FeIV state. A tryptophan positioned between the two hemes in two out of the three known enzymes to form this state, MauG and MbnH, has been proposed as the dominant pathway for interheme electron transfer. .The third enzyme, BthA, instead has a serine at this position. Here, we used site-directed mutagenesis of Trp113 in MbnH to test whether this tryptophan is uniquely required for interheme electron transfer. Computational pathway analysis identified the possibility of an alternative, noncovalent route mediated by Arg283 and a heme propionate with possible electronic coupling comparable to that of the native tryptophan pathway. Consistent with this prediction, only simultaneous disruption of both the tryptophan and propionate-mediated pathways abolished bis-FeIV formation entirely. Moreover, only mutants capable of forming bis-FeIV retained the ability to turnover substrate, directly establishing this high-valent state as the catalytic intermediate responsible for substrate modification. These results demonstrate that an intervening tryptophan is not required for fast interheme electron transfer, and instead reveal an additional, noncovalent pathway that may be a general feature of diheme peroxidases.

missingCandidates.title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

missingCandidates.title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and gt;85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

missingCandidates.title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. missingCandidates.title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

missingCandidates.title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

missingCandidates.title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to gt;20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

missingCandidates.title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

missingCandidates.title: Divergent Assembly of Functionalized Medium-Sized N , O -Heterocycles from N -(2-Hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamide
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The divergent base-mediated formal [4+3] and [4+4] annulation of N-(2-hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamides was described for the preparation of seven- and eight-membered oxazaheterocycles. This strategy exhibited mild conditions, moderate to excellent yields, broad substrate scope, and functional group tolerance. The viability of this synthetic method was confirmed by scale-up reactions and additional transformations. In vitro toxicity experiments revealed that the three kinds of N,O-heterocycles exhibited significant antibacterial activity.

missingCandidates.title: A dual-attribution framework reveals how foreign investment and trade redistribute cobalt availability
A self-limiting mechanotransduction feedback loop ensures robust organ formation

CREST functions as a molecular bridge between neuron-specific enhancers and epigenetic regulators in mature motor neurons
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Motor neuron development requires precise transcriptional regulation mediated in part by BAF (BRG1/BRM-associated factor) chromatin remodeling complexes. The neuron-specific BAF subunit CREST is critical for neuronal function and is mutated in some cases of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), yet its underlying genomic mechanisms remain unclear. Using mouse embryonic stem cell differentiation, we show that CREST is essential for motor neuron maturation by activating mature neuronal genes and repressing progenitor genes. Mechanistically, CREST interacts with the neuronal transcription factors ONECUT1 and NGN2, and the BRM ATPase to target pre-existing accessible enhancers of neuronal genes. CREST deletion selectively prevents CBP histone acetyltransferase recruitment, reducing histone H3K27 acetylation at these enhancers and downregulating target gene expression, without disrupting BRM binding, enhancer accessibility, or long-range chromatin architecture. Overall, our findings identify CREST as a crucial epigenetic mediator bridging lineage-specific transcription factors, BAF complexes, and CBP to activate enhancers and promote proper motor neuron development.

missingCandidates.title: Disability related disparities in diagnosis and survival of digestive system cancers in Northern Italy
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Individuals with disabilities may experience disparities in cancer diagnosis, but population-based evidence remains limited. We conduct a population-based cohort study using linked cancer registry and administrative healthcare data for digestive system cancers diagnosed between 2018 and 2021 in Northern Italy, examining diagnostic routes and one-year survival according to pre-existing impairments. Individuals with impairments are more likely to be diagnosed following emergency presentation compared with those without impairments (51.8% compared with 37.9%; adjusted odds ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval 1.23–1.61), particularly those with impairments of mental and neuromusculoskeletal functions. They also have higher one-year mortality (hazard ratio 1.36, 95% confidence interval 1.26–1.46), independent of socio-demographic and clinical factors. Here, we show that disability-related disparities in emergency cancer diagnosis and survival persist across multiple impairment categories, providing population-based evidence from a European setting on differences in diagnostic pathways across heterogeneous disability groups.

missingCandidates.title: Extensive genomic diversity in Desulfovibrio reveals species-specific functional traits associated with disease
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Desulfovibrio spp. are associated with inflammatory diseases and human health, yet limited representative genomes and isolates hinder our understanding of their role in disease. Here, we assembled a comprehensive database of 2658 Desulfovibrio genomes across 90 diseases and 32 countries, including 24 human isolates. Genomic analyses showed extensive species diversity and revealed disease-associated functional traits, including flagellin and adaptation-associated genes (i.e., ureases). Flagellin-mediated Toll-like receptor 5 activation was species-specific and D. desulfuricans flagellin downregulated TGF-beta signalling in murine small intestinal organoids, suggesting impaired immune tolerance. Additionally, we investigated genomic capacity for hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) production, a main Desulfovibrio metabolite. While health- and disease-associated Desulfovibrio spp. mainly encoded dissimilatory sulfate reduction, tetrathionate metabolism-encoding bacteria were exclusively detected in inflammatory bowel diseases, including Proteus mirabilis and Morganella morganii . Overall, our study provides a comprehensive genomic Desulfovibrio resource and identifies new links associating strain variation, functional traits and H 2 S-production with inflammatory diseases.

missingCandidates.title: Fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography using explicit neural fields
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Multimodal fluorescence and phase imaging provides complementary information about biological samples. However, existing simultaneous fluorescence-phase techniques primarily operate in transmission mode and are limited to thin specimens, restricting their use in thick tissues and in vivo applications. Although multiphoton microscopy enables deep-tissue fluorescence imaging, combining it with three-dimensional refractive-index (RI) imaging remains challenging because few methods can reconstruct the RI of bulky, label-free tissues in reflection mode at subcellular resolution. Here, we introduce fluorescence-illuminated diffraction tomography (FDT), which reconstructs the 3D RI of label-free and fluorescence-labeled objects from diffracted fluorescence images acquired in reflection mode under two-photon excitation. FDT uses the transport of intensity equation and a self-supervised neural network based on explicit neural fields. Compared with state-of-the-art implicit neural fields, this approach improves computational speed, reconstruction accuracy, and interpretability. We demonstrate FDT in two experimental regimes: reconstructing the 3D RI of label-free tissues up to 300 μ m thick placed on a fluorescent substrate, and reconstructing the 3D RI of fluorescence-labeled, 3D-cultured cells without transmission-side access using fluorescence emitted by the cells themselves. FDT establishes a foundation for accessible reflection-mode multimodal fluorescence-phase imaging in complex biological systems.

missingCandidates.title: Fruit-eating adaptations in a Late Cretaceous oviraptorosaur (Theropoda)
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The diversification of herbivorous dinosaurs and the rise of angiosperms in the Late Cretaceous are each well established, but the link between them is debated. Broad-scale diversity patterns in the two groups appear not to closely align, and there is no direct evidence of dinosaur adaptation to angiosperm-based diets. Here we describe Infernogallus jamesi gen. et. sp. nov., a diminutive caenagnathid oviraptorosaur, and show that these theropods were specialised herbivores that originated alongside the rise of fleshy angiosperm fruits. The nearly complete, articulated skull of Infernogallus jamesi —the first for the clade—reveals drastic changes to the adductor musculature organisation, unique in non-avian theropods but converged upon by extant frugivorous parrots. These modifications enabled extensive oral processing of soft food using anteroposterior movement of the mandible and occlusion of ridges and grooves on opposed elements. Altogether, this attests to a highly specialised herbivorous diet in caenagnathids, which likely consisted in large part of fleshy angiosperm fruits, which increased in size and diversity in concert with the radiation of oviraptorosaurs. Caenagnathids thus provide one of the strongest candidates for angiosperm-based diet adaptations in dinosaurs, but their role in the Late Cretaceous proliferation of fruit—which shaped early Cenozoic flora—remains unclear.

H3K27M cooperates with ASCL1 to maintain progenitor states and drive gliomagenesis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Histone 3 lysine 27-to-methionine substitutions (H3K27M) drive aggressive diffuse midline gliomas by blocking differentiation of radial glial progenitor cells committed to oligodendrogenesis. We establish prolonged differentiation as a powerful tool to uncover regulators of glioma cell states and demonstrate that the pioneer transcription factor (TF) ASCL1 is a key mediator of H3K27M-driven plasticity and tumorigenesis. H3K27M prevents Polycomb silencing of ASCL1 , co-opting this TF to maintain oligodendroglial progenitor states. Consistently, ASCL1 loss drastically impairs tumor formation in vivo. Mechanistically, ASCL1 synergizes with H3K27M to redistribute the chromatin remodeler BRG1 to regulatory elements co-enriched for ASCL1 and SOX motifs, promoting expression of stem and neural progenitor genes at the expense of mesenchymal genes in DMGs. ASCL1 loss acts as a “fire exit”, enabling alternative differentiation despite H3K27M, underscoring the therapeutic potential of targeting stalled differentiation and tumor plasticity in histone-mutant gliomas and cancers with a stem cell hierarchy.

missingCandidates.title: Intrinsically flexible inorganic piezoelectric subnanowire enables wireless wearable bioelectronics for non-invasive multimodal human-machine interfacing
Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

missingCandidates.title: Long-term nitrous acid evolution modulates ozone and secondary aerosol variations in global megacities
Preserved higher-order mentalising during strategic interactions after medial prefrontal cortex damage
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Mentalising, the ability to infer the beliefs and intentions of others, is essential for successful social interaction. Previous studies have implicated the medial prefrontal cortex in mentalising, but whether this region is necessary for higher-order mentalising remains unclear. Here we show that people with focal damage to the medial prefrontal cortex retain the ability to engage in higher-order mentalising during a strategic social game. We compare their performance with patients with brain damage in other regions and lesion-free participants. Individuals with medial prefrontal cortex damage achieve similar rewards and use comparable mentalising strategies, but they are slower when making strategic decisions. Computational modelling indicates that this slowing reflects a greater tendency to require evidence before committing to a choice. Voxel-based lesion-symptom mapping identifies medial prefrontal regions linked to altered decision processes rather than mentalising. These findings suggest that the medial prefrontal cortex supports strategic decisions while higher-order mentalising remains intact.

Somatosensory cortex shapes perceptual decision bias via the superior colliculus
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Sensory inputs reach cortical and subcortical areas in parallel, but how they coordinate to guide decisions remains unknown. We examined the roles of the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) and the superior colliculus (SC) in mice performing whisker-mediated tactile detection. While inactivating S1 contralateral to the stimulus increased detection threshold, inactivating ipsilateral S1 decreased it. These opposing effects reflected shifts in choice bias rather than sensitivity. Unilateral SC inactivation produced similar directional effects, whereas bilateral inactivation of either S1 or SC neutralized bias. Furthermore, SC lesions impaired detection performance, and combined S1 inactivation caused no further impairment, indicating that S1-mediated shifts in bias were SC-dependent. S1 inactivation also decreased sensory-evoked neural activity in SC, and choice decoding revealed that behavioral impairment was more closely associated with changes in SC population activity than with loss of sensory encoding in S1. Thus, S1 shapes perceptual bias by modulating SC-dependent circuits that transform sensory evidence into perceptual decisions.

missingCandidates.title: Structural basis of ammonium transport and coordinated regulation of AMT1;1 in Arabidopsis thaliana
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Efficient ammonium uptake is essential for plant growth and nitrogen-use efficiency, yet the structural basis of ammonium transport and regulation in plant AMTs remains unclear. Here, we determined multiple cryo-electron microscopy structures of the Arabidopsis thaliana ammonium transporter AMT1;1 in apo, ammonium-bound, methylammonium-bound, low-pH and phosphomimetic states. These structures reveal a conserved ammonium conduction pathway comprising an aromatic recruitment vestibule, a Phe-gate/Twin-His-containing pore, and a polar intracellular exit region. We further identified a conserved extracellular N-terminal disulfide bond required for oligomer stability and transport activity, suggesting potential redox-dependent regulation. On the cytoplasmic side, phosphorylation modulates C-terminal interactions with intracellular loops, revealing an allosteric regulatory mechanism. Comparison with the bacterial ammonium-sensing protein Sd -Amt1 uncovers a conserved ammonium-recognition region in At AMT1;1 that contributes to transport activity but lacks the signaling module and ligand-dependent conformational switching observed in Sd -Amt1. Together, these findings provide structural insight into ammonium transport and coordinated regulation in plant AMT transporters.

Twisted superconducting quantum diodes for high fidelity anharmonic qubits
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract In superconducting circuits, bidirectional signal propagation can cause back-reflections and back-action that couple environmental noise back to coherent elements, degrading fidelity. Nonreciprocal superconducting diodes provide an intrinsic route to suppress such back-scattering at the circuit level. However, their diode efficiency and quantum integration remain limited. Here, we realize a quantum diode in twisted NbSe 2 under in-plane and out-of-plane magnetic fields. A mere 1 ∘ twist yields an efficiency enhancement over pristine devices, reaching 27.6%. Quantum simulations reveal that this intermediate efficiency, well below 100% ideal, is both experimentally practical and optimal for preserving qubit anharmonicity and stabilizing two-level systems. These findings show that maximal rectification is not always beneficial for quantum information, establishing a new principle for designing the fundamental properties of twisted superconductors towards low-power, high-fidelity quantum circuits.

missingCandidates.title: 1,4-Dioxane as a Sacrificial Radical Buffer Enables Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective C2 Acylation of Indolyl Ketoximes: Access to 2,3-Diacylindoles and Indole-Fused Heterocycles
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Pd-catalyzed regioselective C2 acylation of indoles has been achieved using a C3-ketoxime directing group and glyoxal/aldehydes. The protocol provides C2 acylated indoles with high selectivity and enables one-pot access to indole-fused pyridazines and 2,3-diacylindoles. Mechanistic studies revealed that 1,4-dioxane acts not only as solvent but also as a sacrificial radical buffer that modulates TBHP derived tBuO• and tBuOO• species. Thereby suppressing undesired side reactions while facilitating the desired acylation pathway.

missingCandidates.title: Chiral 1,2-Benzothiazine Synthesis via Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Activation/Cyclization with Chiral Carboxylic Amides
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Chiral sulfur-containing fused heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry. Expanding the catalytic repertoire for the asymmetric synthesis of bioactive sulfur heterocycles via C–H activation remains a persistent pursuit. We report herein an efficient annulation of sulfoximines with diarylacetylenes catalyzed by an achiral Cp*Rh(III) complex, where stereocontrol is governed by a chiral carboxylic amide additive. This protocol provides access to a diverse array of enantioenriched 1,2-benzothiazines in excellent yields (up to 99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee).

missingCandidates.title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Photochemical enantioselective nickel catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent decarboxylative cross-coupling of α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to enantioenriched α-aryl ketones. The reaction selectively engages two structurally distinct carboxylic acid-derived coupling partners while suppressing competing protodecarboxylation and homocoupling pathways. This protocol features broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee), providing a modular and practical approach to chiral α-aryl ketones from readily accessible carboxylic acid feedstocks.

missingCandidates.title: Enantioselective Benzylic C–H Insertions with Diazosuccinate Esters
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The first enantioselective benzylic C–H insertion using α-alkyl-α-diazoesters, facilitated by a well-established chiral dirhodium(II) catalyst, is presented. This reaction selectively functionalizes primary benzylic C–H bonds with good to excellent enantioselectivity (up to 95% ee), thereby demonstrating the synthetic utility of this previously underexplored class of diazo reagents. The resulting differentiated diester products undergo selective monoester removal, thereby enabling subsequent functional-group manipulation of the liberated carboxylic acid and expanding access to enantioenriched building blocks.

missingCandidates.title: Synthesis of the N -Alkoxyguanidinyl Spiroketal Core of Rugonidines A–F
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract Rugonidines A–F are a family of structurally unique diastereomeric alkaloids characterized by an unprecedented [4.5]-fused N-alkoxyguanidinyl spiroketal ring system. This work reports the first synthesis of this motif via an acid-catalyzed, one-pot tandem deprotection/cyclization cascade of a protected N-hydroxyguanidine intermediate, efficiently forging the target spirocyclic framework in 21% yield over nine steps. X-ray crystallographic analysis unambiguously confirmed structural connectivity, providing the first solid-state characterization of this unusual architecture.

missingCandidates.title: Transient-Directing Group-Enabled Manganese-Catalyzed C–H Alkylation
missingCandidates.abstract: Abstract The construction of C–C bonds by manganese-catalyzed C–H activation thus far relies on permanent directing groups that need to be installed and removed, while the use of transient directing groups remains an elusive challenge. In sharp contrast, we herein describe a manganese-catalyzed intramolecular C–H alkylation of indole-3-carboxaldehydes enabled by the use of a transient directing group in catalytic quantities. Our strategy provided access to a wide range of N1/C2-fused polycyclic indoles, generating a tertiary C-center in excellent yields and concomitant good functional group tolerance. The desired polycyclic indole underwent late-stage diversification guided by the native formyl directing group through C4–H activation, as well as leading to the decoration with barbituric acid moiety. Additionally, computational mechanistic insight by DFT provided support for a rate-determining migratory insertion.

missingCandidates.title: Catechol as a Co‐Polymerization Mediator for Programmable Surface Chemistry Structure Synthesis of Carbon Dots
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Red‐emissive carbon dots (R‐CDs) hold promise for bioimaging and optoelectronics, yet their synthesis under mild, scalable conditions remains challenging. Conventional hydrothermal routes demand high temperature and pressure, while ambient‐pressure alternatives rely on strong acids and yield limited quantum yields without programmable surface control. This work reports a catechol‐assisted ambient‐pressure strategy that achieves hundred‐gram‐scale preparation of R‐CDs by simple heating at ∼90°C. Catechol acts as a co‐polymerization mediator, participating in formation of carbon dots while its dual hydrogen‐bonding network suppresses functional‐group detachment, stabilizes radical intermediates, and lowers the steric barrier for cyclization. This mechanism enables programmable tuning of hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity and emission wavelength by varying the precursor substituents. The hydrophobic carbon dots exhibit a solid‐state quantum yield of 45.26% (encapsulated in polyvinylpyrrolidone), the highest reported, and enable white light‐emitting diodes (WLED) with a color rendering index (CRI) of 94. The hydrophilic carbon dots (quantum yield 37.86%) are directly applied to deep‐tissue in vivo imaging without surface modification. This work provides a versatile molecular engineering platform for sustainable synthesis of functional aromatic carbon nanomaterials.

missingCandidates.title: Enhanced Electrochemical C–N Coupling for Glycine Synthesis via an Active Hydrogen Pump
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct electrochemical C–N coupling of abundant carbon and nitrogen feedstocks offers a sustainable route to glycine synthesis, yet achieving high efficiency remains challenging. Here, we develop an In–Bi catalyst by incorporating oxophilic indium (In) into a bismuth (Bi) matrix. During the co‐reduction of oxalic acid and NO 3 − , the In–Bi catalyst delivers an exceptional Faradaic efficiency toward glycine (FE Glycine ) of 83.3% with an industrial‐level current density of 361.3 mA cm −2 , together with a glycine production rate of 4.3 mol h −1 g cat. −1 . It outperforms pristine Bi and previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Large‐scale glycine electrosynthesis is further demonstrated over a 10 cm 2 In–Bi electrode, achieving a total current of 1.5 A with FE Glycine of 68.5% and yielding 1.4 g of glycine in 6 h. Mechanistically, oxalic acid and NO 3 − first form glyoxylic acid oxime (GAO). Subsequently, In sites act as an “active hydrogen pump” to accelerate H 2 O dissociation, providing abundant surface‐active hydrogen (*H) for efficient GAO hydrogenation to glycine. Meanwhile, the incorporation of In modulates the electronic structure of the Bi matrix, enhancing GAO adsorption and electron transfer. The synergistic regulation of *H supply and electronic structure accelerates the conversion of GAO to glycine, resulting in superior performance of In–Bi.

missingCandidates.title: Light‐Driven Control of Polar Order in Ferroelectric Nematic Liquid Crystals
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Ferroelectric nematic (N F ) liquid crystals are polar fluids that combine long‐range orientational order with spontaneous macroscopic polarization and exceptionally large dielectric permittivity. While these properties make N F materials attractive for responsive soft devices, incorporating additional functionality remains challenging because polar order is highly sensitive to molecular mismatch. Here we introduce a molecular design strategy that enables optical control of N F materials using azobenzene‐based mesogens structurally matched to the archetypal N F compound DIO. Two derivatives are themselves ferroelectric nematogens, demonstrating that photoisomerizable mesogens can intrinsically sustain and modulate N F polar order, with large and reversible light‐induced changes in polarization and dielectric permittivity. The same structural matching principle also enables non‐N F azobenzenes to co‐assemble with DIO at concentrations up to 20 wt.% while preserving ferroelectric nematic order. In selected blends, light irradiation drives a reversible transition from the ferroelectric nematic state to a low‐permittivity state consistent with antiferroelectric smectic order. Together, light and temperature provide complementary handles to navigate this phase landscape of competing ferroelectric and antiferroelectric order. These results provide a molecular design strategy for programming collective polar order in ferroelectric nematic fluids using light‐responsive mesogens.

missingCandidates.title: Macrocyclization of ω‐Isocyano Aldehydes
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Medium‐sized rings and macrocycles constitute a privileged class of scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, providing unique access to challenging biological targets through their preorganized, semi‐rigid architectures. However, their synthesis remains challenging due to the unfavorable kinetic and thermodynamic constraints during ring closure. Herein, we report the efficient cyclization of ω‐isocyano aldehydes via Passerini and Ugi multicomponent reactions (MCRs), alongside related variants. These transformations provide rapid access to structurally diverse medium‐sized and macrocyclic α‐acyloxy, α‐hydroxy, α‐acetamido, and α‐keto lactams, as well as tetrazole‐fused macrocycles, under mild conditions. Notably, this macrocyclization strategy relies on C(sp 3 )─C(sp 2 ) bond formation while simultaneously generating α‐functionalized amide motifs. By avoiding the need to pre‐synthesize α‐functionalized carboxylic acids, this approach offers a complementary alternative to traditional macrolactamization.

missingCandidates.title: Mortise‐and‐Tenon Molecular Joint Covalent Organic Frameworks With Tunable Topology for Photothermal‐Catalytic Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The controllable regulation of dimensionality and interpenetration in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is crucial for optimizing photocatalytic performance, yet the translation of 3D COFs from structural construction to functional customization remains challenging. Here, we successfully designed a series of mortise‐and‐tenon molecular joint COFs by rationally engineering a twisted tetraphthaldehyde ligand bearing π‐conjugated “clips”. Stepwise extension of the “clips” enables topological evolution from 2D to twofold interpenetrated 3D, and ultimately to noninterpenetrated 3D structure. Notably, DHP‐CuPor‐COF with noninterpenetrated 3D structure amplifies light‐harvesting efficiency and substrate accessibility, enabling superior photothermal conversion and catalytic performance over its 2D and twofold interpenetrated 3D counterparts. To the best of our knowledge, it delivers highly efficient photothermal‐catalytic C─X (X = O, S) bond formation for selective transformation of phenolic compounds via cross‐dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reactions (conv., 90% and yield, 80%), markedly outperforming conventional thermal catalysis. The high efficiency arises from the synergistic of open 3D channels, abundant Cu‐porphyrin active sites and strong photothermal effect. This work provides an innovative strategy to tune the topological chemistry of COFs for advanced photocatalytic applications.

missingCandidates.title: Nature of C─N Coupling in Urea Electrosynthesis for Catalyst Design
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic co‐reduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − offers a low‐carbon route to urea, yet practical deployment is constrained by unsatisfactory efficiency due to the absence of a quantitative, theory‐guided catalyst design principle. In this study, we propose the generalized dipole moment (GDM) of active sites as a transferable descriptor guided by charge‐locking asymmetric site polarization (CLASP) mechanism, that can quantify polarization strength correlated with selectivity prediction for catalysts. Constant‐potential simulations show that increasing GDM strengthens *CO 2 adsorption, promotes H 2 O dissociation, and progressively favors C─N coupling relative to the competing protonation pathway. The slow‐growth method further tracks charge evolution along the *CO─*NO coupling coordinate, confirming that polarized active sites precharge *CO and facilitate the predominant C‐to‐N charge‐redistribution tendency during formation of critical coupling intermediates. Guided by this descriptor, a series of Ln─Cu alloy catalysts were designed to validate the predicted scaling, with La─Cu as the best candidate.

missingCandidates.title: S = 3/2 Iron(I)‐Bisphosphine‐Ate Complexes: Synthesis, Characterization, and Reactivity for Electrophile Activation
missingCandidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Iron bisphosphine complexes represent an important class of sustainable catalysts for a variety of important chemical transformations due to the high abundance, low toxicity, and redox‐rich chemistry inherent to iron‐based systems. In particular, transient, low‐coordinate Fe(I) species are postulated to play a pivotal role in multiple catalytic transformations as the principal species for C─X bond activation (X = Cl, Br, I). However, insight into the electronic structure, bonding, and reactivity of Fe(I)‐bisphosphine complexes remains poorly developed. In the present study, we report the development of four‐coordinate (4C), high‐spin ( S = 3/2) Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates. Several novel Fe(I) complexes were structurally characterized, and their electronic structure and bonding were evaluated using a combined spectroscopic, synthetic, and computational approach. Additionally, this study highlights the potential role of charged species in synthetically relevant contexts via in situ formation of (4C) Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates in the presence of ubiquitous additives (e.g. MgBr 2 ). Lastly, we demonstrate the utility of these Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates toward rapid C─X homolytic cleavage of common alkyl‐ and aryl‐halide electrophiles, as well as the ability to serve as synthons for further development of new high‐spin Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ate complexes through transmetalation.

potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Metallo-β-lactamases (MBLs) are key contributors to antimicrobial resistance (AMR). The L1 MBL, originally from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, is a tetrameric, dizinc, subclass B3 MBL that efficiently hydrolyzes most β-lactam antibiotics and evades inhibitors that act on other MBLs. Using quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (DFTB3/MM) simulations with enhanced sampling, we mapped the full reaction pathway and minimum free energy profile for L1-catalyzed hydrolysis of faropenem, a penem antibiotic whose reaction can yield alternative enamine and imine products. We test different possible mechanisms and find that changes in hydration at the metal site during the catalytic cycle are critical for efficient hydrolysis. The direct reaction of EI, however, involves a large energy barrier; the second stage is facilitated by diffusion of a water molecule into the active site. Direct proton transfer from this water to the substrate amide nitrogen forms an enamine product, while imine formation requires rotation of the faropenem 6α-hydroxyethyl substituent to enable proton transfer from water to the substrate C2.
