potentialGaps.title: Biomarker and Bioorthogonality Dual‐Locked Chemiluminescent Probes for Cancer Urine Test
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Bioorthogonality‐activatable optical imaging activates caged or quenched probes via bioorthogonal reactions for disease diagnosis. Although chemiluminescence enables low‐background detection, it has rarely been applied to bioorthogonality‐activatable imaging. Here, we synthesize chemiluminescent tetrazine probes (CLTZs) by coupling a tetrazine acceptor to a phenoxy‐1,2‐dioxetane donor through π‐conjugated vinylene linkers, enabling biomarker and bioorthogonality dual‐locked activation for cancer urine testing. Unlike conventional chemiluminophores, tetrazine in CLTZs mediates an internal‐conversion‐to‐a‐dark‐state quenching mechanism, suppressing chemiluminescence even after phenolate formation. Strong chemiluminescence is restored only when the phenolate form undergoes bioorthogonal reaction with bicyclononyne (BCN), generating pyridazine‐containing donor–π–acceptor chemiluminophores. This unique dark state enables development of an H 2 O 2 and bioorthogonality dual‐locked probe ( H BCP), emitting only when both H 2 O 2 and BCN are present. By engineering BCN into a cancer‐activatable bioorthogonal urinary reporter ( C BUR) that releases renal‐clearable BCN in tumors, a chemiluminescent bioorthogonal pair ( H BCP C BUR) is created. This pair achieves in vivo tumor imaging with a signal‐to‐background ratio of 438 and detects lung metastasis in early urinary assays with up to 23.9‐fold signal enhancement over healthy mice. This work provides a molecular design for bioorthogonality‐activatable chemiluminescence toward noninvasive, sensitive disease diagnosis.

potentialGaps.title: Controlled Hydrogen Delivery by Single‐Atom Ru Accelerates Electrocatalytic Ammonia Synthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic nitric oxide reduction to ammonia (NORR) offers a dual opportunity for NO remediation and decentralized NH 3 production, yet its efficiency is often limited by competing pathways and unclear structure–function relationships. Here we introduce a reactant‐shunting strategy that installs a guiding electrocatalytic step via isolated Ru atoms to supply surface‐bound * H species and enforce a Langmuir–Hinshelwood (LH) hydrogenation pathway. Using Ru 1 /Co 3 O 4 as a model catalyst, we show that single Ru sites promote water adsorption and dissociation, forming stable Ru‐H intermediates that thermodynamically and kinetically accelerate the coupling‐hydrogenation steps in NORR. The optimized catalyst delivers an NH 3 yield of 533.49 µmol cm −2 h −1 with a 97.19% faradaic efficiency, surpassing state‐of‐the‐art systems. The reactant‐shunting principle further generalizes across multiple oxide hosts, enhancing NH 3 productivity by up to threefold. These findings establish pathway steering through controlled hydrogen delivery as a powerful strategy for high‐efficiency electrocatalytic ammonia synthesis.

potentialGaps.title: Double Reduction of Ph 3 B to a Dianionic Borane With a Powerful Sr I Intermediate
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Reduction of [(BDI)SrI] 2 with KC 8 generated in situ a (BDI)Sr I species which enabled the reduction of Ph 3 B to the Ph 3 B 2− dianion (BDI = HC[(Me)C═N‐DIPeP] 2 , DIPeP = 2,6‐(Et 2 CH) 2 ‐phenyl). The product (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) features a Ph 3 B 2− dianion that is bridging two Sr 2+ cations by interaction with one of the Ph rings. This polarizes a large part of the electron density in the bridging Ph ring (NPA charge: −1.53) whereas the B is slightly positive (+0.44). The HOMO of the complex mainly consists of the π*‐orbital in the bridging Ph ring overlapping with Sr d ‐orbitals. However, there is also 18% contribution of the B p ‐orbital. In solution, there is coalescence of 1 H NMR signals of all three Ph rings. Complex (BDI)Sr(BPh 3 )Sr(BDI) can react as a 2 e transfer reagent or as a B‐nucleophile. It reacts with I 2 to Ph 3 B and [(BDI)SrI] 2 . Reaction with Ph 3 B led to formation of a Gomberg‐type dimer. The reaction with PhI is smooth and selectively gave (BDI)Sr(Ph 4 B) and [(BDI)SrI] 2 , likely through direct nucleophilic attack of an electron rich B atom at PhI. Isolation of a complex with the elusive Ph 3 B 2− dianion demonstrates the very high reducing power of in situ generated (BDI)Sr I species.

potentialGaps.title: In Situ and Operando Techniques for Electrocatalysis in Renewable Energy Applications
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalysis is essential for renewable energy conversion, yet the mechanisms governing catalytic performance remain poorly understood due to the complex nature of electrochemical interfaces. Advances in nanomaterial synthesis and high‐resolution characterization now allow detailed structural and compositional analysis, but static methods fall short of capturing the dynamic behaviors of active sites during operation. In this review, we focus on the growing role of in situ and operando techniques such as optical, X‐ray, and electron‐based, in resolving catalytic structure and reactivity under real‐life working conditions. These methods offer unparalleled access to the evolution of surface species, reaction intermediates, and interfacial topologies that govern catalytic functions. We highlight how in situ and operando studies have revealed transient phenomena and mechanistic details previously inaccessible, and discuss their critical roles in advancing systems for water splitting, CO 2 /N 2 reduction, and fuel cells related renewable energy applications. Beyond highlighting the real‐time transformations captured by operando and in situ methods, this review underscores how coupling operando datasets with theoretical modeling and machine learning can accelerate mechanistic discovery and enable rational catalyst design. By extracting hidden correlations and guiding closed‐loop experimentation, data‐driven approaches promise to reduce reliance on empirical trial‐and‐error and unlock predictive control over catalytic performance. Taken together, these developments position operando characterization, when coupled with AI‐driven interpretation, as a cornerstone of future energy research, providing a pathway to accelerate discovery, design, and deployment of next‐gen

potentialGaps.title: Modular Construction of Cyclic and Linear Quaternary Carbon Centers through Visible‐Light‐Induced Triplet Nitrene Transfer Reaction
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT All‐carbon quaternary centers represent a fundamental structural unit found in a wide range of functional molecules. Within the versatile synthetic toolbox, the semipinacol rearrangement (SPR) stands as one of the most powerful tools for assembling this sterically congested motif. In this context, ‌radical‐mediated SPR pathways‌, especially those entailing alkyl migrations, remain underexplored from a strategic standpoint. Herein, we report a visible light‐promoted formal SPR of tertiary allyl alcohols using in situ‐generated triplet nitrene species as the initiator under redox‐neutral conditions. This method demonstrates broad substrate scope, enabling efficient construction of all‐carbon quaternary centers across various steric environments, including rigid cyclic/spiro frameworks and flexible acyclic systems. Mechanistic investigations reveal substrate‐dependent pathways: alkenyl cyclobutanols undergo triplet nitrene addition followed by concurrent ring‐expansion and hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) to form cyclic ketones, while nonactivated allyl alcohols proceed through aziridination/ring‐opening/SPR sequences to produce linear β‐amino ketones. Preliminary biological assessments of these α‐quaternary β‐aminoketone derivatives revealed that compound 4a exhibited potent anti‐DENV‐2 activity, with an EC 50 value of 0.95 ± 0.02 µM against viral replication.

potentialGaps.title: Overcoming the Spin Barrier of Oxygen Redox Chemistry in Lithium–Oxygen Batteries via Metal–Support Magnetic Interaction
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT A major bottleneck for the practical application of lithium–oxygen (Li–O 2 ) batteries is the high overpotential resulting from sluggish kinetics of oxygen redox chemistry. This kinetic limitation can rise in part from the spin‐state transition barriers in converting triplet oxygen ( 3 O 2 ) into peroxide species, alongside the parasitic generation of singlet oxygen ( 1 O 2 ). Here, we demonstrate that metal–support magnetic interactions can effectively overcome this spin barrier. Using palladium (Pd) nanoparticles anchored on ferrimagnetic CoFe 2 O 4 (CFO) substrates as a model catalyst, we reveal that interfacial magnetic coupling restructures the spin and electronic states of Pd sites, generating spin‐polarized active ensembles with optimized adsorption toward oxygen intermediates. This interfacial spin‐electronic effect promotes the conversion of 3 O 2 into peroxide species while suppressing parasitic 1 O 2 evolution during charging, thereby improving the reversibility of oxygen redox chemistry. As a result, the Pd/CFO catalyst achieves a low charging overpotential of 0.05 V and remarkable energy efficiency (91.2%) under spin alignment. This finding establishes metal–support magnetic interaction as a powerful strategy for controlling spin‐dependent oxygen electrocatalysis, providing a general design principle for catalysts involving multi‐site interactions.

potentialGaps.title: Persistent Mn 3+ Sites on Reduced MnO Enable Efficient Syngas Conversion
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Mn‐based materials are widely used for syngas conversion, where MnO is generally regarded as the catalytically active phase under reducing conditions. Yet catalysts derived from different Mn oxide precursors often exhibit markedly different performances despite evolving into the same MnO bulk structure during reaction. Here we show that trace Mn 3+ sites stabilized on oxygen‐deficient MnO surfaces serve as the decisive active sites. Time‐resolved energy‐dispersive x‐ray absorption spectroscopy combined with iterative target transformation factor analysis and depth‐resolved synchrotron photoemission spectroscopy reveals a persistent minor Mn 3 O 4 ‐like spectral contribution and its enrichment near the surface of Mn 2 O 3 ‐derived MnO. These stabilized sites strongly enhance CO adsorption and activation, thereby promoting C─O bond cleavage and markedly improving activity and selectivity for syngas‐to‐light‐olefin conversion. More broadly, this work reveals how minority surface sites can govern catalytic function despite identical bulk phases and establishes an operando strategy for quantitatively resolving low‐coverage active sites in reducible oxide catalysts.

potentialGaps.title: RNA Organelles in DNA‐Based Artificial Cells Provide Spatial Aptamer Functions and Enhanced Signal Processing
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Naturally occurring biomolecular condensates orchestrate key cellular processes by creating spatially distinct reaction environments, yet engineering synthetic condensates that combine structural programmability with spatioselectively encoded function remains challenging. Here, we report multiphase DNA–RNA artificial cells (ACs) that embed functional RNA condensates as organelle‐like compartments within programmable DNA core–shell ACs. A single thermal assembly protocol yields three‐phase ACs comprising a glassy RNA core organelle embedded in a liquid‐like DNA compartment, surrounded by a crosslinked DNA shell. The RNA organelles contain aptamer function, enabling selective protein recruitment and small‐molecule activation, while the DNA scaffold provides independent addressability, modulates RNA‐condensate size, and enhances resistance to serum‐mediated degradation. We further show that RNA chemistry can be used to adjust environmental responsiveness: unmodified RNA organelles undergo rapid degradation in serum and release captured protein cargo, whereas 2′‐fluoro‐modified RNA organelles remain stable for at least 24 h. Finally, by coupling transcriptional modules localized in the DNA core to cell‐free protein translation in the surrounding medium, we establish sender–receiver communication between AC populations and self‐actuating signal processing within individual DNA–RNA ACs. These results establish hybrid nucleic‐acid ACs as programmable, spatially organized systems that couple compartment architecture, RNA molecular recognition, and biochemical communication.

potentialGaps.title: Stabilizing Functional Nucleic Acids for Real‐Sample Diagnostics
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Functional nucleic acids (FNAs), including aptamers and DNAzymes, offer programmable recognition and catalysis for biosensing, but their performance in real samples is often compromised by nuclease degradation, matrix effects, and interface‐associated losses. For diagnostic translation, stability must, therefore, be defined not only as strand persistence, but as retained folding, binding, catalysis, and signal generation under assay‐relevant conditions. This review examines strategies for stabilizing FNAs in complex biological matrices and organizes the field around four design levers: Chemical, topological, architectural, and microenvironment/interface engineering. Chemical modification of sugars, backbones, and bases can reduce nuclease susceptibility, but requires functional validation. Topological approaches, including terminus shielding, circularization, covalent locking, and mechanically interlocked structures, limit strand accessibility, and reinforce functional conformations. Architectural strategies use multivalency, scaffolded presentation, DNA nanostructures, and rolling circle amplification‐derived concatemers to improve robustness and signal retention. Microenvironment engineering further stabilizes FNAs through controlled immobilization, antifouling interfaces, nanomaterial‐assisted protection, hydrogel or microgel confinement, and sample processing. Case studies in saliva, serum, urine, and stool illustrate how these levers can be combined to enable reliable FNA‐based real‐sample diagnostics.

potentialGaps.title: Birch-Type-Reduced Carbazole Anions Enable Redox-Adaptive Super-Reducing Photocatalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Photocatalytic activation of inert chemical bonds is constrained by the redox potential of the catalyst. Here, we report a redox-adaptive photocatalytic strategy in which an electron-rich carbazole photocatalyst, CBZ6, functions as a molecular redox transformer through the formation of Birch-type carbazole anions. Under visible light, CBZ6 switches between a neutral state for conventional photoredox reactions and an anionic state for super-reducing catalysis. Excitation of the anionic state generates a super-reducing species with an excited-state oxidation potential of approximately −3.6 V versus SCE, substantially beyond that of the neutral excited state (−2.2 V). This adaptive redox switching enables activation of otherwise inaccessible C–F bonds in aryl fluorides, polyfluoroalkyl compounds, and fluoropolymers. The complementary reactivities of the two states further enable diverse photoredox transformations, establishing redox adaptation as a strategy for expanding the accessible reactivity of organic photocatalysts.

potentialGaps.title: Cesium-Induced Stabilization of the FeOOH Cocatalyst on Bismuth Vanadate Photoanode for Ultraefficient and Stable Photoelectrochemical Water Oxidation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Developing active and durable water oxidation cocatalysts is essential for advancing photoelectrochemical (PEC) water-splitting systems. This study investigates the cesium-induced reconstruction of the FeOOH cocatalyst on a bismuth vanadate (BVO) photoanode for the water oxidation reaction, with a focus on the reconstruction process and its effect in improving interfacial charge transfer and photostability. Cesium ions induce the reconstruction of Fe species on the BVO/FeOOH photoanode during the PEC process, leading to the formation of a robust Cs-incorporated FeOOH (Cs:FeOOH) catalytic layer. Spectroscopic analysis combined with open-circuit potential measurement reveals that the in situ formed Cs:FeOOH cocatalyst can effectively protect BVO and promote interfacial hole transfer during PEC operation. As a result, the BVO/Cs:FeOOH photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 6.29 mA cm–2 at 1.23 V vs. RHE and maintains stable operation for over 100 h. Furthermore, the Cs-incorporated FeOOH cocatalyst strategy can be extended to other semiconductor systems, including TiO2 and FeOx, highlighting its broader potential for improving solar-driven PEC water oxidation.

potentialGaps.title: Circular RNA Delivery In Vitro and In Vivo Using Doubly Branched Aminoethoxy-Functionalized Ionizable Lipid Nanoparticles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Circular RNA is a therapeutically promising RNA modality with superior stability and extended protein expression relative to linear RNA. While delivery systems for linear RNA have received much attention, less effort has been directed toward the delivery of circular RNA, whose closed topology and physicochemical properties differ from those of linear RNAs. Here, we disclose a class of ionizable lipids that enable efficient in vitro and in vivo delivery of circular RNA. These ionizable lipids are step-economically accessible, allowing facile assessment of their structure–delivery relationships. Our studies reveal key elements that enhance circular RNA delivery in vitro and in vivo, including aminoethoxy head units, doubly branched tails and linkers tuned for hydrogen bonding and biodegradability. The lead ionizable lipid for circular RNA delivery, iL-19, incorporating these features, achieves ∼28-fold higher protein expression in C2C12 myocytes than Moderna’s SM-102 formulation and 2.5-fold higher expression upon intramuscular administration in BALB/c mice. iL-19 also surpasses benchmark ionizable lipids ALC-0315 (7.8-fold) and DLin-MC3-DMA (33.4-fold) for intramuscular circular RNA delivery in vivo under otherwise identical conditions. This study establishes design principles and a step-economical synthesis for accessing ionizable lipids that enable highly efficient in vitro and in vivo circular RNA delivery.

potentialGaps.title: Electroanalytical and Computational Investigation of Oxoammonium-Mediated Hydride Transfer
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer is an important yet relatively underexplored elementary step in C–H functionalization. In this work, we employed cyclic voltammetry (CV) to measure the rates of hydride transfer between electrochemically generated oxoammonium catalysts and 42 substrates including ethers, carbamates, amides, and sulfonamides. Through quantum mechanical (QM) calculations, we uncovered a new transition-state model for hydride transfer in which the N atom of the catalyst resides near a heteroatom (X = N or O) of the substrate to allow alignment of the oxoammonium’s O═N+ motif and the substrate’s forming C═X+ bond. Energy decomposition analysis was subsequently performed to elucidate the key factors that govern the kinetics of oxoammonium-mediated hydride transfer. Beyond conventional electronic and steric considerations, we identified substrate distortion, secondary orbital interactions, and noncovalent interactions as critical factors that influence hydride transfer reactivity. We anticipate that these kinetic data along with the mechanistic insights they provide will inform future catalyst development and synthetic applications to broaden the scope of oxoammonium catalysis.

potentialGaps.title: Engineering a Reconfigurable Transmembrane Receptor Enables Logic-Controlled Signal Translocation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Transmembrane receptors relay extracellular cues into intracellular responses through reconfigurable conformational changes, yet engineering synthetic systems that emulate receptor-like signal translocation with programmable control remains challenging. Here, we engineer a reconfigurable transmembrane receptor that enables logic-controlled signal translocation across lipid membranes. The receptor is constructed from an oriented Y-shaped triplex DNA architecture that inserts directionally into the plasma membrane via dual cholesterol anchors and integrates two environmental inputs─H+ and ATP─through an i-motif and an aptamer module. Under dual-input conditions, cooperative duplex-to-triplex switching triggers reconfigurable structural rearrangement and drives transmembrane relocation of a signaling strand from the outer to the inner membrane leaflet. This receptor-mediated signal translocation converts extracellular chemical cues into spatially defined intracellular activation. The repositioned strand serves as a modular intracellular effector that can be functionalized to implement programmable reactions, including bioorthogonal catalysis and light-triggered photocatalysis at the membrane interface. Importantly, endogenous tumor-microenvironmental cues trigger receptor reconfiguration and signal translocation in 3D tumor spheroids and in vivo, enabling logic-gated intracellular photocatalysis and gt;85% tumor growth inhibition in xenograft models. By coupling logic-gated reconfigurable switching with directional transmembrane signal propagation, this work establishes an engineered transmembrane receptor for programmable intracellular activation and provides a general strategy for synthetic signal translocation in living systems.

potentialGaps.title: Hydrogenation of CO2 to Propane and n -Butane by Engineering Metal Oxide Interfacial Structure and Manipulating Zeolite Pore Structure and Acidity
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Selective hydrogenation of CO2 to propane and n-butane is of great interest, as these two compounds are not only primary components of liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) but also crucial raw materials for preparing propene and a degradable plastic precursor of succinic acid. Although various composite catalysts combining metal oxides and zeolites have been explored, their catalytic performances remain insufficient. Here, we found that ZnZrOx decorated with ultrasmall FeOx clusters, forming an intimate FeOx–ZnZrOx interfacial structure, showed high catalytic activity for CO2 hydrogenation to methanol due to a strong CO2 adsorption capacity and H2 dissociation ability, and silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieve with RHO topological structure enhanced methanol conversion into propane and n-butane via hexamethylbenzenes as active hydrocarbon pool species owing to its unique supercage structure and double eight-membered ring pore opening. As a result, coupling of these two materials delivers a CO2 conversion of ∼66% and a (propane + n-butane) selectivity of 82% in hydrocarbons, which leads to a (propane + n-butane) yield of ∼42%. It is surprising that this composite preferentially produces n-butane rather than iso-butane, and the n-butane/iso-butane ratio is higher than 85.8. The high catalytic stability of this composite is demonstrated by maintaining CO2 conversion, (propane + n-butane) selectivity in hydrocarbons, and their yield of ∼ 61%, ∼ 77%, and ∼ 31%, respectively, after a reaction of 620 h. This work not only fabricates a high-performance catalyst for CO2 hydrogenation to propane and n-butane by engineering the metal oxide interfacial structure and manipulating the zeolite’s pore structure and acidity, but also makes it possible to develop an efficient way for

potentialGaps.title: Metal Fluorides: All-In-One Supports for Ruthenium-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Ammonia, an emerging energy carrier, demands advanced catalysts for synthesis under mild conditions to integrate with green hydrogen. We herein establish a family of metal fluoride supports (MFn, M = Li, Na, K, Mg, Ca, or Ba) as a tunable “all-in-one” platform for ruthenium (Ru) catalysts. These Ru/MFn systems unify the critical merits of various existing catalysts, such as support-mediated activation of reactants and air stability. Varying the host cation can direct the catalytic pathway. Consequently, Ru/NaF exhibits excellent turnover frequency, while Ru/BaF2 delivers an NH3 synthesis rate of 58.0 mmolNH3 gcat–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 0.9 MPa─surpassing all reported Ru-based catalysts with ≤4 wt % Ru and without external promoters. Advanced characterization reveals that the fluorine vacancy formation energies of the alkali and alkaline-earth lattices, together with the vacancy-reactant interactions, dictate the divergent catalytic mechanisms mediated by different active sites. This work expands the chemistry of metal fluorides, launching a new paradigm for potentially viable NH3-synthesis under mild conditions.

potentialGaps.title: NMR Spectroscopic Evidence for Magnetically Induced Ring Currents in All-Metal-Aromatic [Bi4]4+
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Experimental assignment of aromaticity in all-metal systems remains challenging, particularly for heavy-element clusters, where local magnetic effects can obscure signatures of circular electron delocalization. Here, we investigate a supramolecularly stabilized, formally tetracationic [Bi4]4+ ring by combining structurally meaningful reference compounds, solid- and solution-state NMR spectroscopy, SQUID magnetometry, and exact two-component relativistic calculations. Comparison with an isostructural [Li4Br]3+-encapsulated analogue and a binuclear Bi(III) reference compound disentangles global ring-current effects from local heavy-atom deshielding and ligand-specific conformational effects. On this basis, the unusually downfield-shifted 1H and 13C NMR signals observed for the Bi4-containing species provide direct spectroscopic evidence for magnetically induced ring currents in the [Bi4]4+ core. By contrast, bulk magnetic measurements do not reveal significant diamagnetic exaltation, indicating that this quantity is not a resolved descriptor of aromaticity in these systems. Stoichiometric studies further identify chemically competent intermediates that provide mechanistic snapshots of [Bi4]4+ ring formation. Complementary calculations support the assignment of a magnetically responsive, σ-delocalized [Bi4]4+ core, reproduce a rare spectroscopically observed puckering motion of the rhomboidal [Bi4]4+, and underscore the critical role of spin–orbit coupling on electronic structure and dynamics. Overall, this work moves the discussion of aromaticity from predominantly computational assignment toward experimentally benchmarked analysis in the heavy-element and all-metal regime.

potentialGaps.title: Regio- and Enantioselective Functionalization of Gaseous Alkanes via Nickel-Catalyzed Alkene Dicarbofunctionalization
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The regio- and enantioselective functionalization of gaseous alkanes remains an unsolved challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a general strategy for the asymmetric three-component dicarbofunctionalization of alkenes using readily available gaseous alkanes, including ethane, propane, and isobutane. This transformation, enabled by the merger of hydrogen atom transfer photocatalysis with a chiral nickel catalyst, efficiently delivers chiral α-aryl carbonyl compounds in good yield with excellent regio- and enantioselectivity (up to gt;20:1 rr and 99:1 er). Experimental and computational studies reveal insights into the mechanism controlling selectivity. Operating under exceptionally mild, energy-efficient conditions, the method unlocks a versatile platform for upgrading feedstock gaseous alkanes into sought-after chiral building blocks.

potentialGaps.title: Selective Consecutive Decarboxylation Enables Skeletal Contraction of Waste PET
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Direct catalytic upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) to benzene through consecutive decarboxylation contracts the terephthalate-derived C8 framework to C6, representing a skeletal-editing strategy for aromatic polycarboxylates. The key challenge is to control pathway selection across consecutive decarboxylation steps, favoring sequential aryl–carboxyl C–C bond cleavage over competing hydrogenolysis while preserving the aromatic core. Herein, we report an efficient direct catalytic conversion of waste PET to benzene, achieving an exceptionally high yield of 83.3% over a tailored Ru/W0.4ZrOx catalyst. The performance arises from synergistic acid-site reconstruction and oxygen-vacancy engineering. Moderate WOx incorporation into ZrO2 converts Lewis acidity into Brønsted acidity, while oxygen vacancies and WOx species promote adsorption and activation of carboxyl groups. In cooperation with Ru nanoparticles, these features preferentially stabilize the decarboxylation intermediate over its hydrogenolysis counterpart, directing both consecutive steps toward C–C bond cleavage while suppressing undesired hydrogenolysis pathways. Controlled hydrogen supply and a deliberately designed dodecane/water mixed solvent system further enhance selectivity. The catalyst performs effectively across diverse real-world PET wastes, with preliminary techno-economic and life-cycle analyses indicating favorable process-level metrics under the evaluated assumptions. More broadly, these mechanistic insights establish synergistic acidity and oxygen-vacancy regulation as a catalyst-design principle for decarboxylative skeletal editing of aromatic polycarboxylates.

potentialGaps.title: Divergent Assembly of Functionalized Medium-Sized N , O -Heterocycles from N -(2-Hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamide
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The divergent base-mediated formal [4+3] and [4+4] annulation of N-(2-hydroxyethyl)sulfonylamides was described for the preparation of seven- and eight-membered oxazaheterocycles. This strategy exhibited mild conditions, moderate to excellent yields, broad substrate scope, and functional group tolerance. The viability of this synthetic method was confirmed by scale-up reactions and additional transformations. In vitro toxicity experiments revealed that the three kinds of N,O-heterocycles exhibited significant antibacterial activity.

potentialGaps.title: Large-scale identical-location electron microscopy enables quantifying nanoparticulate electrocatalyst degradation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Fuel cells convert chemical energy into electricity, and their performance relies on electrocatalysts whose durability during operation remains poorly understood. Deep mechanistic insight into electrocatalyst stability is essential to design durable, resource-efficient fuel cells. Nanoparticulate electrocatalysts degrade via diverse nanoscale processes, yet particle-to-particle heterogeneity in structure, support interaction, and local microenvironment make true particle-level quantification and understanding impossible with classical approaches. Here we scale up identical-location scanning transmission electron microscopy, which repeatedly images the very same nanoparticles, to track the structural evolution of hundreds of carbon-supported platinum-cobalt nanoparticles, a prototypical oxygen reduction reaction electrocatalyst. We present a three-step image analysis workflow comprising segmentation, tracking, and degradation-event classification with progressive automation, including machine-learning-assisted detection of overlapping particles. By pairing nanoscale resolution and local history with population-level statistics, the pipeline enables unbiased identification and quantification of degradation pathways across statistically meaningful particle sets. We reveal particle size- and shape-dependent effects, showing that smaller and irregular nanoparticles are more prone to detachment, and provide a data-driven framework for probing electrocatalyst degradation at scale.

potentialGaps.title: 1,4-Dioxane as a Sacrificial Radical Buffer Enables Pd-Catalyzed Regioselective C2 Acylation of Indolyl Ketoximes: Access to 2,3-Diacylindoles and Indole-Fused Heterocycles
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Pd-catalyzed regioselective C2 acylation of indoles has been achieved using a C3-ketoxime directing group and glyoxal/aldehydes. The protocol provides C2 acylated indoles with high selectivity and enables one-pot access to indole-fused pyridazines and 2,3-diacylindoles. Mechanistic studies revealed that 1,4-dioxane acts not only as solvent but also as a sacrificial radical buffer that modulates TBHP derived tBuO• and tBuOO• species. Thereby suppressing undesired side reactions while facilitating the desired acylation pathway.

potentialGaps.title: Chiral 1,2-Benzothiazine Synthesis via Rhodium-Catalyzed Asymmetric C–H Activation/Cyclization with Chiral Carboxylic Amides
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Chiral sulfur-containing fused heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry. Expanding the catalytic repertoire for the asymmetric synthesis of bioactive sulfur heterocycles via C–H activation remains a persistent pursuit. We report herein an efficient annulation of sulfoximines with diarylacetylenes catalyzed by an achiral Cp*Rh(III) complex, where stereocontrol is governed by a chiral carboxylic amide additive. This protocol provides access to a diverse array of enantioenriched 1,2-benzothiazines in excellent yields (up to 99%) and enantioselectivities (up to 99% ee).

potentialGaps.title: Enantioconvergent Decarboxylative Cross-Coupling for the Synthesis of α-Aryl Ketones via Metallaphotoredox Catalysis
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Photochemical enantioselective nickel catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for constructing stereogenic C(sp3)–C(sp2) bonds in organic synthesis and medicinal chemistry. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent decarboxylative cross-coupling of α-aryl carboxylic acid derivatives with aliphatic carboxylic acids, providing efficient access to enantioenriched α-aryl ketones. The reaction selectively engages two structurally distinct carboxylic acid-derived coupling partners while suppressing competing protodecarboxylation and homocoupling pathways. This protocol features broad substrate scope, good functional group tolerance, and excellent enantioselectivity (up to 98% ee), providing a modular and practical approach to chiral α-aryl ketones from readily accessible carboxylic acid feedstocks.

potentialGaps.title: Enantioselective Benzylic C–H Insertions with Diazosuccinate Esters
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The first enantioselective benzylic C–H insertion using α-alkyl-α-diazoesters, facilitated by a well-established chiral dirhodium(II) catalyst, is presented. This reaction selectively functionalizes primary benzylic C–H bonds with good to excellent enantioselectivity (up to 95% ee), thereby demonstrating the synthetic utility of this previously underexplored class of diazo reagents. The resulting differentiated diester products undergo selective monoester removal, thereby enabling subsequent functional-group manipulation of the liberated carboxylic acid and expanding access to enantioenriched building blocks.

potentialGaps.title: Synthesis of the N -Alkoxyguanidinyl Spiroketal Core of Rugonidines A–F
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract Rugonidines A–F are a family of structurally unique diastereomeric alkaloids characterized by an unprecedented [4.5]-fused N-alkoxyguanidinyl spiroketal ring system. This work reports the first synthesis of this motif via an acid-catalyzed, one-pot tandem deprotection/cyclization cascade of a protected N-hydroxyguanidine intermediate, efficiently forging the target spirocyclic framework in 21% yield over nine steps. X-ray crystallographic analysis unambiguously confirmed structural connectivity, providing the first solid-state characterization of this unusual architecture.

potentialGaps.title: Transient-Directing Group-Enabled Manganese-Catalyzed C–H Alkylation
potentialGaps.abstract: Abstract The construction of C–C bonds by manganese-catalyzed C–H activation thus far relies on permanent directing groups that need to be installed and removed, while the use of transient directing groups remains an elusive challenge. In sharp contrast, we herein describe a manganese-catalyzed intramolecular C–H alkylation of indole-3-carboxaldehydes enabled by the use of a transient directing group in catalytic quantities. Our strategy provided access to a wide range of N1/C2-fused polycyclic indoles, generating a tertiary C-center in excellent yields and concomitant good functional group tolerance. The desired polycyclic indole underwent late-stage diversification guided by the native formyl directing group through C4–H activation, as well as leading to the decoration with barbituric acid moiety. Additionally, computational mechanistic insight by DFT provided support for a rate-determining migratory insertion.

potentialGaps.title: Catechol as a Co‐Polymerization Mediator for Programmable Surface Chemistry Structure Synthesis of Carbon Dots
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Red‐emissive carbon dots (R‐CDs) hold promise for bioimaging and optoelectronics, yet their synthesis under mild, scalable conditions remains challenging. Conventional hydrothermal routes demand high temperature and pressure, while ambient‐pressure alternatives rely on strong acids and yield limited quantum yields without programmable surface control. This work reports a catechol‐assisted ambient‐pressure strategy that achieves hundred‐gram‐scale preparation of R‐CDs by simple heating at ∼90°C. Catechol acts as a co‐polymerization mediator, participating in formation of carbon dots while its dual hydrogen‐bonding network suppresses functional‐group detachment, stabilizes radical intermediates, and lowers the steric barrier for cyclization. This mechanism enables programmable tuning of hydrophilicity/hydrophobicity and emission wavelength by varying the precursor substituents. The hydrophobic carbon dots exhibit a solid‐state quantum yield of 45.26% (encapsulated in polyvinylpyrrolidone), the highest reported, and enable white light‐emitting diodes (WLED) with a color rendering index (CRI) of 94. The hydrophilic carbon dots (quantum yield 37.86%) are directly applied to deep‐tissue in vivo imaging without surface modification. This work provides a versatile molecular engineering platform for sustainable synthesis of functional aromatic carbon nanomaterials.

potentialGaps.title: Enhanced Electrochemical C–N Coupling for Glycine Synthesis via an Active Hydrogen Pump
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Direct electrochemical C–N coupling of abundant carbon and nitrogen feedstocks offers a sustainable route to glycine synthesis, yet achieving high efficiency remains challenging. Here, we develop an In–Bi catalyst by incorporating oxophilic indium (In) into a bismuth (Bi) matrix. During the co‐reduction of oxalic acid and NO 3 − , the In–Bi catalyst delivers an exceptional Faradaic efficiency toward glycine (FE Glycine ) of 83.3% with an industrial‐level current density of 361.3 mA cm −2 , together with a glycine production rate of 4.3 mol h −1 g cat. −1 . It outperforms pristine Bi and previously reported state‐of‐the‐art catalysts. Large‐scale glycine electrosynthesis is further demonstrated over a 10 cm 2 In–Bi electrode, achieving a total current of 1.5 A with FE Glycine of 68.5% and yielding 1.4 g of glycine in 6 h. Mechanistically, oxalic acid and NO 3 − first form glyoxylic acid oxime (GAO). Subsequently, In sites act as an “active hydrogen pump” to accelerate H 2 O dissociation, providing abundant surface‐active hydrogen (*H) for efficient GAO hydrogenation to glycine. Meanwhile, the incorporation of In modulates the electronic structure of the Bi matrix, enhancing GAO adsorption and electron transfer. The synergistic regulation of *H supply and electronic structure accelerates the conversion of GAO to glycine, resulting in superior performance of In–Bi.

potentialGaps.title: Macrocyclization of ω‐Isocyano Aldehydes
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Medium‐sized rings and macrocycles constitute a privileged class of scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, providing unique access to challenging biological targets through their preorganized, semi‐rigid architectures. However, their synthesis remains challenging due to the unfavorable kinetic and thermodynamic constraints during ring closure. Herein, we report the efficient cyclization of ω‐isocyano aldehydes via Passerini and Ugi multicomponent reactions (MCRs), alongside related variants. These transformations provide rapid access to structurally diverse medium‐sized and macrocyclic α‐acyloxy, α‐hydroxy, α‐acetamido, and α‐keto lactams, as well as tetrazole‐fused macrocycles, under mild conditions. Notably, this macrocyclization strategy relies on C(sp 3 )─C(sp 2 ) bond formation while simultaneously generating α‐functionalized amide motifs. By avoiding the need to pre‐synthesize α‐functionalized carboxylic acids, this approach offers a complementary alternative to traditional macrolactamization.

potentialGaps.title: Mortise‐and‐Tenon Molecular Joint Covalent Organic Frameworks With Tunable Topology for Photothermal‐Catalytic Cross‐Dehydrogenative Coupling
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT The controllable regulation of dimensionality and interpenetration in covalent organic frameworks (COFs) is crucial for optimizing photocatalytic performance, yet the translation of 3D COFs from structural construction to functional customization remains challenging. Here, we successfully designed a series of mortise‐and‐tenon molecular joint COFs by rationally engineering a twisted tetraphthaldehyde ligand bearing π‐conjugated “clips”. Stepwise extension of the “clips” enables topological evolution from 2D to twofold interpenetrated 3D, and ultimately to noninterpenetrated 3D structure. Notably, DHP‐CuPor‐COF with noninterpenetrated 3D structure amplifies light‐harvesting efficiency and substrate accessibility, enabling superior photothermal conversion and catalytic performance over its 2D and twofold interpenetrated 3D counterparts. To the best of our knowledge, it delivers highly efficient photothermal‐catalytic C─X (X = O, S) bond formation for selective transformation of phenolic compounds via cross‐dehydrogenative coupling (CDC) reactions (conv., 90% and yield, 80%), markedly outperforming conventional thermal catalysis. The high efficiency arises from the synergistic of open 3D channels, abundant Cu‐porphyrin active sites and strong photothermal effect. This work provides an innovative strategy to tune the topological chemistry of COFs for advanced photocatalytic applications.

potentialGaps.title: Nature of C─N Coupling in Urea Electrosynthesis for Catalyst Design
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic co‐reduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − offers a low‐carbon route to urea, yet practical deployment is constrained by unsatisfactory efficiency due to the absence of a quantitative, theory‐guided catalyst design principle. In this study, we propose the generalized dipole moment (GDM) of active sites as a transferable descriptor guided by charge‐locking asymmetric site polarization (CLASP) mechanism, that can quantify polarization strength correlated with selectivity prediction for catalysts. Constant‐potential simulations show that increasing GDM strengthens *CO 2 adsorption, promotes H 2 O dissociation, and progressively favors C─N coupling relative to the competing protonation pathway. The slow‐growth method further tracks charge evolution along the *CO─*NO coupling coordinate, confirming that polarized active sites precharge *CO and facilitate the predominant C‐to‐N charge‐redistribution tendency during formation of critical coupling intermediates. Guided by this descriptor, a series of Ln─Cu alloy catalysts were designed to validate the predicted scaling, with La─Cu as the best candidate.

potentialGaps.title: S = 3/2 Iron(I)‐Bisphosphine‐Ate Complexes: Synthesis, Characterization, and Reactivity for Electrophile Activation
potentialGaps.abstract: ABSTRACT Iron bisphosphine complexes represent an important class of sustainable catalysts for a variety of important chemical transformations due to the high abundance, low toxicity, and redox‐rich chemistry inherent to iron‐based systems. In particular, transient, low‐coordinate Fe(I) species are postulated to play a pivotal role in multiple catalytic transformations as the principal species for C─X bond activation (X = Cl, Br, I). However, insight into the electronic structure, bonding, and reactivity of Fe(I)‐bisphosphine complexes remains poorly developed. In the present study, we report the development of four‐coordinate (4C), high‐spin ( S = 3/2) Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates. Several novel Fe(I) complexes were structurally characterized, and their electronic structure and bonding were evaluated using a combined spectroscopic, synthetic, and computational approach. Additionally, this study highlights the potential role of charged species in synthetically relevant contexts via in situ formation of (4C) Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates in the presence of ubiquitous additives (e.g. MgBr 2 ). Lastly, we demonstrate the utility of these Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ates toward rapid C─X homolytic cleavage of common alkyl‐ and aryl‐halide electrophiles, as well as the ability to serve as synthons for further development of new high‐spin Fe(I)‐bisphosphine‐ate complexes through transmetalation.
